messages.content: is only i read the page the same as i read only one page?
no. only i read the page is about who read that page. i read only one page is about how many pages you read.
can i use both ideas together?
only i read that page, and i read only one page.
does that mean the other people read no pages?
no. they could have read other pages. only i read that page is about that specific page.
make that answer shorter.
they could have read other pages, just not that page.
now make it about my sister reading only one page.
my sister read only one page.
why not only my sister read one page?
that would change the question to who did that reading, rather than only how many pages your sister read.
only give that page sentence again.
my sister read only one page.
write a longer story about two empty containers that look the same. one is for food and one is for paper, and a child asks before choosing.

a child was asked to put some paper away. on the shelf, he saw two empty containers of the same size and color. he took the one near his hand, then stopped because he remembered his mother using one for food. he asked which one was for paper. she showed him the one to use and explained that the other was kept for food. being empty had not made both containers ready for the same task. the child put his paper in the right one and left the food container where it was. later, he wrote a short word on a page and kept it with his paper so the use would be clear next time too.
what made the containers hard to choose between?
they were the same size and color, and both were empty.
why did he ask before putting the paper in?
he knew one was used for food and did not know which one was right for paper.
make the important choice in the story more simple.
he asked about the use of each container instead of choosing by how close it was.
can empty tell you every use an object is ready for?
no. you may need to know what it is for and other details about it.
finish with his paper easy to find.
he put the container back on the shelf and left the page with it. the next day, he knew where his drawing paper was.
my friend told the first part of a story before we had to leave. i want to ask for the rest another time, not right now.
i would like to hear the rest of the story when you have time.
can i make it sound like i remembered what they told me?
i keep thinking about the story you started. i would like to hear the rest when you have time.
what if i do not want to say i keep thinking about it?
then leave that out. you can simply say you would like to hear more without adding a feeling you did not give.
only give the first sentence again.
i would like to hear the rest of the story when you have time.
does that mean they must write it all down?
no. the message does not choose writing. it can mean talking another time, unless you give a more specific request.
only ask about talking another day.
would you like to tell me the rest of the story another day?
can return the book and give the book back mean the same thing?
yes. both can be about taking a book back to the person or place it came from.
can return also mean a person going back?
yes. i will return home after lunch is about you going home again, not giving an object back.
make a sentence with both ideas.
i will return home and give the book back to my sister.
can you use return for both without changing the meaning?
i will return home and return the book to my sister.
only give that sentence again.
i will return home and return the book to my sister.
can you know my sister is home?
not from that sentence alone. it gives your plan, but not where she is now.
make that explanation shorter.
it does not give where she is now.
yesterday was busy. today i want something quiet, but i do not want to make a whole plan.
we can keep it small. would you rather read, sit outside, or just talk for a little while?
just talk. i do not want another list of things to do.
okay. what part of yesterday is still on your mind?
the visit with my cousin. it was good, just long.
you can have liked the visit and still want less talking today.
can you say that more simply?
you can have a good visit and need quiet later.
make that sentence about both feelings.
you can enjoy the visit and need quiet after it.
now just give a kind reply without another question.
you do not need to make today busy to make it useful.
five children had a page to read. not all finished. does that mean nobody finished?
no. it says the whole group did not all finish. it does not say nobody finished.
make that explanation shorter.
not all is different from nobody.
now i say three finished. how many did not?
two did not finish.
can not all finished still be true?
yes. two did not finish, so not all finished is true.
can nobody finished be true with that information?
no. three finished.
only give the number who did finish.
three.
what if those last two finish later?
then all five have finished by that later time. the first answer can still be true for its own time.
write a longer story about someone saying the page is finished and another person not knowing whether it has been read or written. keep reading and writing clear.

a child came to his sister and said the page was finished. she put it with the paper to return to their teacher, thinking he had finished writing his answer. he stopped her and explained that he was talking about finishing reading the page the teacher gave them. his own answer had not been written yet. they took the page back to the table and kept the reading and writing in different places. after that, he said finished reading or finished writing to make clear which part was done. the added word was short, but it changed what his sister could do with the page. she did not need to ask every detail once she knew which task he was talking about.
what did he mean by finished at first?
he was talking about finishing the reading.
what did his sister think?
she thought he had finished writing his answer.
make the important idea one sentence.
adding reading or writing made clear which part was done.
write a more clear sentence for the child.
i have finished reading the page, but i still need to write my answer.
finish with the writing task ready to begin.
he put a clean page next to the book and wrote the first sentence of his answer.
i need the table in the evening, but my sister can choose when to draw before that. help me say both.
i need the table this evening. you can use it for drawing before then, at a time that works for you.
can you ask if that is enough time?
i need the table this evening. would using it before then give you enough time to draw?
what if she says no?
then you can talk about another place or time. with a question, she can say whether the plan works for her.
make that explanation shorter.
asking gives room for her answer too.
now only give my need, without choosing for her.
i need the table this evening.
can you know why?
no. you gave the need, but not the task you will use it for.
only give the question again.
would using the table before this evening give you enough time to draw?
is how far is the library the same as how long does the walk take?
no. how far asks how much road or space is between the places. how long asks how much time the walk takes.
make that explanation shorter.
how far is about space. how long is about time in these questions.
can two people take different time for the same road?
yes. one may walk fast while the other walks slowly, or one may stop for a break.
make that answer shorter.
yes. one could stop for a break while the other keeps walking.
only give that idea without yes.
one could stop for a break while the other keeps walking.
now ask only about the time from home to the library.
how long does it take to walk from home to the library?
can you answer without knowing the place?
not with a specific time. i would need the places and something about the walk.
write a longer story about a child answering five and then learning that a person who came late does not know what five is about.

a child was looking at books at the table with his father. when his sister came in, he said five. she thought he was telling her the time, because she had asked when they would leave. his father asked the child to give the whole answer. he said there were five books on the table. now his sister knew it was not about their journey. they still needed to check the time for leaving. the same number could have been part of many answers, and the person coming in did not hear the question that made it clear. later, the child said both the number and what it was about when talking to someone new.
what was five really about?
the number of books on the table.
why did his sister think it was a time?
she had been asking about when they would leave.
make that answer more general.
she heard the number without hearing the question before it.
write the full answer that made it clear.
there are five books on the table.
finish with the time still being checked as its own question.
his father looked at the clock and answered the leaving question. the child kept the books in their group on the table.
i wrote one sentence and then knew what the next part of my story could be.
one sentence can give you a start for the next, even if you have not chosen the whole story yet.
make that reply shorter.
the first sentence can help you choose the next.
can i keep the next part open until i write more?
yes. you do not need every choice made before writing a first sentence, unless your task asks for a full plan first.
help me say that in one sentence.
i can begin with one clear sentence and choose more of the story as i write.
does that say plans are always wrong?
no. it says this way of starting can work. a plan may help with another task.
make that explanation shorter.
plans can help too. this is another possible way to begin.
only give my sentence again.
i can begin with one clear sentence and choose more of the story as i write.
my sentence is clear but a little long. help me make it shorter without changing the meaning: i will call you after i get home from the library.
i will call you after getting home from the library.
did you make it much shorter?
only one word shorter. keeping home is useful if that part of the time is important.
give that explanation more simply.
keep getting home in the message if that detail is important.
make that reply shorter.
do not leave out an important detail just to make it shorter.
only give the clear sentence again.
i will call you after i get home from the library.
why did you keep the original?
because it already gives your meaning clearly. making it shorter is not useful if the person might lose an important detail.
can this book and that book be about the same book at different parts of a conversation?
yes. when the book is near you, you may say this book. from another place, someone may say that book about it.
make that explanation shorter.
both can be about the same book from a different place or person.
can you know they are different books just from those words?
not without context. they can be about the same book or two different books.
make that explanation shorter.
context is needed to know whether it is one book or two.
now make a sentence saying both people mean one book.
we are both talking about the same book.
only give that sentence again.
we are both talking about the same book.
my sister has a book, and i have a book too. can you know there are two different books?
not for sure. you might each have a different book, or you might mean the same book you share.
now i say i took mine from the shelf and she took hers from the table, and they are different books.
then there are two different books.
if we put both on the same table, do they become one book?
no. putting two objects together does not make them one object.
what if both have the same story?
then two books can hold the same story.
make that answer more clear with two and one.
two books can be two objects with one story in both.
only give how many different books there are from my clear detail.
two different books.
can you know who bought them?
no. you have not given that information.
my friend asked which part i needed help with, and that helped me know. give me a short thank you.
thank you. that question helped me find the part i needed.
can you make it shorter?
thank you for asking that.
does that say they wrote the answer for me?
no. it thanks them for the question, not for writing the answer.
only give a goodbye in two words.
take care.
i want to write about living in a house near the moon. do not make that a fact about where i live.
we can keep it as a made up story. the house can be part of that story, not your real home.
write one first sentence using i.
i lived in a small house with the moon close outside my window.
make the house red.
i lived in a small red house with the moon close outside my window.
can you know that is my memory?
no. you asked for a made up first sentence, so it is not a memory you gave.
now make it about a girl instead of i.
a girl lived in a small house with the moon close outside her window.
only give a simple hello from you now.
hello.
